original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.

actual_scope: Eliminate the measured whole-fixture deepcopy bottleneck in all 32 retained R2 semantic mutation tests with source-specific path copies; compare with unchanged deepcopy and the credited checked-marshal baseline.
scope_change_reason: Explicit user optimization assignment follows PR3218 remaining-cost handoff. Profiling identified whole-fixture mutation copying as the dominant cost; the task does not change mathematical predicates or the comparator.
bottleneck_link: Faster complete audits make the existing source/event/native failure checks cheaper to run and review without dropping mutants.
stop_rule: Session 2026-10-17T18:23:43Z to 19:23:43Z; final 15 minutes for verification and handoff. Stop on any full-mutant, named-rejection, original-fixture-isolation or source-binding discrepancy. One exact two-provider caller only.
evidence: BENCHMARK.json records nine fresh serial runs: 5.365x complete-audit speedup over deepcopy and 1.691x over the credited checked-marshal baseline. RESULT.json records all 32 complete mutant/deepcopy equalities, all original named rejections and 253 identical operator decisions. PROOF.md gives the source-specific write-footprint argument.
author: Tekalign (@tekuuu)
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in profiling, implementation, proof, tests, benchmarking and writing; no independent human/proof-kernel review.

open_questions.question: Can another current audit prove a similarly narrow mutation write footprint?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Large mutable fixtures can make fault injection more expensive than the actual predicates.
open_questions.first_step: Profile a named source-pinned caller, list actual mutation writes, compare every complete optimized mutant with original deepcopy, and benchmark against checked marshal.
open_questions.blocked_by: No generic alias-safe deepcopy replacement or other-caller speedup is established.

open_questions.question: Can the remaining R2 frame/event replay be accelerated without caching acceptance?
open_questions.why_it_matters: After eliminating fixture copies, repeated source/event reconstruction becomes the main cost.
open_questions.first_step: Profile the unchanged predicates, then prove any frame-value reuse preserves type/rank checks and complete invalidation.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package intentionally changes only mutation isolation; no event acceptance or frame cache is introduced.
